Air pollution — GRAP, CAQM.page: Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), Mechanism, Stages, Challenges
facts: GRAP followed Supreme Court directions in M.C. Mehta vs Union of India (2016) and was notified by MoEFCC in 2017.
It was first implemented by EPCA under the Environment Protection Act, 1986; CAQM has executed it since 2021.
GRAP is incremental: earlier-stage measures stay in force as AQI worsens; IMD and SAFAR forecasts trigger preventive action.

facts: 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 added the Tenth Schedule; the 91st Amendment, 2003 omitted the split exception.
Kihoto Hollohan: presiding officer acts as a tribunal; decision reviewable on grounds of mala fides or perversity.
Critics call it contradictory that an Independent joining a party is disqualified while a nominated member may join.
Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990): disqualification to be decided by President/Governor on Election Commission’s advice.

Arbitration — enforcement of foreign awa.page: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Features, Major Provisions
facts: An arbitral award is enforceable like a court decree under Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
Awards can be set aside under Section 34 only on limited grounds such as incapacity or invalid agreement.
The 2021 amendment removed automatic stays on awards, reinforcing a pro-enforcement approach.
Section 29A sets a 12-month time limit for domestic arbitral awards.

Bonded labour — rehabilitation, 1976 Act.page: Bonded Labour Act, Status, Provisions, Reasons & Measures
facts: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 abolishes bonded labour, frees workers from debt obligations and makes forced work illegal.
Vigilance committees at district, sub-division and block levels identify, rescue and help rehabilitate bonded labourers.
Article 23 bars traffic in human beings, begar and forced labour; Bandhua Mukti Morcha (1984) directed States to identify, release and rehabilitate.

Brahmaputra — Siang Upper Multipurpose P.page: Siang Dam Controversy: China, Hydropower and Indigenous Rights
facts: SUMP is an 11,200 MW project on the Siang, potentially India’s largest hydropower project, at the pre-feasibility stage.
It is meant to counter China’s 60,000 MW dam at Medog on the Yarlung Tsangpo; the Siang is the Brahmaputra’s upper course.
The Adi tribe, who call the river ‘Ane Siang’, fear loss of homes, farmland and cultural heritage.
NHPC and NEEPCO are the developers; Upper Siang Stage-I and II were merged into one project in 2017.

Census 2027 — caste enumeration.page: Understanding SECC 2011 and India's Caste Census Landscape
facts: SECC 2011 was a joint exercise with Census 2011 but administratively distinct, under MHA through the Registrar General of India.
Census 2011 asked only SC/ST status, not specific caste names or OBC category.
The 1941 Census collected caste data, but it was not released due to World War II.

Chola bronzes — Nataraja, lost-wax.page: Imperial Cholas: Art, Architecture and Literature
facts: Nataraja's matted locks represent the Ganga; one male and one female earring denote Ardhanarishwara.
A snake around Shiva's arm symbolises kundalini power; the nimbus of lights denotes unending cycles of time.
Chola paintings were executed on walls, murals and wooden panels inside temples.

facts: CAA covers Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered by 31 December 2014.
It relaxed the naturalisation residency requirement from 11 years to 6 years for these communities.
Sixth Schedule areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Tripura and Inner Line Permit areas are exempt.
MHA notified CAA Rules in 2024; applications go online to district-level and empowered committees.

Civil aviation — Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhin.page: Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak 2024, Features, Criticisms, and Implications for India’s Aviation Sector
facts: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaces the Aircraft Act, 1934, which had been amended 21 times.
It provides for three authorities: DGCA (safety regulation), BCAS (security) and AAIB (accident investigation).
Appeals against DGCA or BCAS orders lie with the Central government; critics note the DGCA is not an independent regulator.

Content blocking — Sec 69A, 79(3)(b), IT.page: Government Tightens Online Content Blocking Rules, Adds Senior-Level Oversight
facts: Only Joint Secretary or DIG-rank officers and above can issue blocking notices under Section 79(3)(b).
Section 79(3)(b) covers unlawful content broadly; Section 69A applies to threats to sovereignty, defence or security.
A Rule 3(1)(d) notice removes safe-harbour for flagged content unless the platform justifies or removes it.

Cyber fraud — digital arrest, mule accou.page: Digital Arrest Fraud in India, Supreme Court Action and RBI Reforms
facts: Digital arrest is not a separate offence under Indian law at present.
SC took suo motu cognisance in October 2025 after a complaint from a senior citizen couple from Haryana.
SC directed the CBI to investigate major digital arrest cases, including frauds of ₹10 crore or more.

Data protection — DPDP Act, AI training.page: DPDP Act 2023, DPDP Rules 2025, Objectives, Provisions
facts: DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified on 14 November 2025, operationalising the DPDP Act, 2023.
Penalties: up to ₹250 crore for failing to prevent breaches, up to ₹200 crore for breach non-reporting or children’s data violations.
The Data Protection Board of India handles grievances and enforcement; its members are appointed by the Central Government.
Significant Data Fiduciaries face audits and impact assessments; verifiable parental consent is needed for children’s data.

Challenges: political opposition, employee resistance, undervaluation in weak markets and loss of future dividends.
Disinvestment gained importance after the 1991 LPG reforms to mobilise resources and improve PSU efficiency.

Drug trafficking — Punjab, Golden Cresce.page: Drug Trafficking, Causes, Effects, Laws in India, Government Measures
facts: North-western border States Punjab, J&K and parts of Rajasthan and Gujarat face cross-border smuggling challenges.
Nar-K9 Pool uses trained dogs to detect narcotics; darknet and cryptocurrency monitoring tracks online drug transactions.
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan promotes awareness; NAPDDR supports prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration.

Electoral rolls — SIR, Form 7 deletions.page: Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Meaning, Phases, Latest News 2026
facts: Article 324 vests superintendence of electoral rolls in the ECI; Article 326 provides elections on adult suffrage.
RPA 1950: Section 16 disqualifies non-citizens from registration; Section 19 links registration to age and ordinary residence.
SIR Phase II covered 12 States/UTs with about 50.99 crore electors; earlier intensive revisions ran up to 2002-2004.

Energy security — crude import sourcing.page: India's Energy Security Amid Global Conflicts
facts: India imports over 85% of its crude oil; nearly 25% of global oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz.
Russia's share rose from 2% before 2022 to nearly 36% in FY2024-25, making it India's largest supplier.
Suggested path: larger Strategic Petroleum Reserves, lower oil intensity, maritime security and a critical mineral ecosystem.

Firecracker regulation — green crackers,.page: Green Crackers, Meaning, Features, Latest News
facts: Green crackers were developed by CSIR-NEERI after the Supreme Court banned conventional firecrackers; they exclude barium compounds.
Three types exist: SWAS (Safe Water Releaser), STAR (Safe Thermite Cracker) and SAFAL (Safe Minimal Aluminium).
They cut particulate matter, SO2 and NO2 emissions by at least 30 per cent compared with conventional crackers.
The October 2018 Arjun Gopal order banned all crackers except green ones; the NGT imposed an absolute ban in the NCR in November 2020.

GLOF — transboundary early warning.page: India's Preparedness Against Glacial Lake Outburst Floods
facts: NDMA's $20 million national programme identifies 195 high-risk glacial lakes in four vulnerability levels.
India has over 7,500 glacial lakes across 11 river basins.
Supraglacial lakes form on the glacier surface and are vulnerable to summer melting.

facts: GST Council was established under Article 279A by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
Article 279A(9): decisions need at least three-fourths of weighted votes of members present and voting.
Article 279A(5) lets the Council recommend the date for GST on petroleum, diesel, petrol, natural gas and aviation fuel.

Gig workers — Code on Social Security, 2.page: Code on Social Security 2020, Need, Provisions, Significance
facts: The Code received Presidential assent on 28 September 2020 and came into force on 21 November 2025.
Fixed-term employees become eligible for gratuity after one year of continuous service.
Unorganised, gig and platform workers register on a National Portal and receive a Unique Identification Number.

India–China border — LAC, 2005 Agreement.page: India China Relations, History, Timeline, UPSC Notes
facts: India acknowledges the McMahon Line in the eastern sector; China does not recognise it.
The 2022 Yangtse clash in Arunachal Pradesh saw around 300 Chinese troops advance near Chumi Gyatse Falls.
Border States/UTs: Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh; the boundary is not fully demarcated.

Israel–Palestine — UN Commission of Inqu.page: Israel Palestine Conflict - History, War Timeline, Map, Reasons
facts: Oslo Accords: mutual recognition of Israel and PLO; five-year interim Palestinian self-government in Gaza and the West Bank.
Oslo II divided the West Bank into Areas A (Palestinian control), B (joint) and C (Israeli control).
India voted in 2017 against unilateral recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital and supports a two-state solution.

NavIC — NVS series.page: IRNSS-NavIC: Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System
facts: NavIC uses three satellites in GSO and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit; it became operational in 2018.
Expected position accuracy is better than 20 m in the primary service area.
Second-generation satellites carry a Rubidium atomic clock developed by the Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad.

Poverty estimation — World Bank brief, M.page: Issues Relating to Poverty in India, Estimation
facts: Poverty lines in India are based on consumption expenditure, not income; the basket is the Poverty Line Basket (PLB).
Tendulkar Committee (2009): 2011-12 line of Rs 816 rural and Rs 1,000 urban per capita per month.
Rangarajan Committee (2014): Rs 972 rural and Rs 1,407 urban monthly per capita expenditure.
Lakdawala (1993) suggested State-specific lines; Alagh Committee (1979) set nutrition-based rural and urban lines.

Prison reforms — overcrowding, Model Pri.page: Resolving the Issue of Overcrowded Prisons in India
facts: As of December 31, 2022, prisons had 131% occupancy: 5,73,220 inmates against capacity of 4,36,266.
Undertrial prisoners constitute 75.7% of the total inmate population.
SC's Centre for Research and Planning recommends phased electronic monitoring of low and moderate-risk undertrials.

Renewable energy — rooftop solar, PM Sur.page: Renewable Energy in India, Sectors, Initiatives, Significance
facts: PM Surya Ghar targets rooftop solar in one crore households with a ₹75,021 crore outlay.
India’s installed renewable capacity, including large hydro, was about 299.25 GW as of 30 September 2026.
Other schemes: PM-KUSUM, National Green Hydrogen Mission, PLI for solar PV modules and Green Energy Corridor.

Rural employment — VB-G RAM G, grievance.page: VB-G RAM G to Replace MGNREGS: Key Changes in Rural Employment Scheme
facts: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 replaces MGNREGA from 1 July 2026 and raises the guarantee from 100 to 125 days a year.
A 60-day pause during peak sowing and harvesting seasons is built in to keep farm labour available.
The Centre now fixes normative State allocations (top-down) and may withhold a share for performance, including social audit compliance.
Funding is shared between Centre and States (60:40 or 90:10); eight sets of draft rules were released.

State Election Commission — Art 243K, vo.page: State Election Commission, Provisions, Powers, Functions, Reforms
facts: Article 243K vests superintendence, direction and control of Panchayat rolls and elections in the SEC; Article 243ZA does so for Municipalities.
The Governor appoints the State Election Commissioner; removal only as for a High Court judge.
The SEC enforces the Model Code of Conduct in local elections and carries out delimitation of local-body constituencies.

State Legislative Councils — Arts 168-17.page: State Legislative Council in India, Articles, Eligibility, Election
facts: Article 169 lets Parliament create or abolish a Council after the Assembly passes a resolution by special majority; it is not binding on Parliament.
Six States have Councils: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh.
Strength is at most one-third of the Assembly and at least 40; members must be at least 30 years old.
The Council of Ministers is not collectively responsible to the Council; it cannot pass a no-confidence motion.

Stubble burning — paddy residue, Punjab.page: Stubble Burning in India: Causes, Laws and Policy Solutions
facts: Stubble burning in Punjab began in the late 1970s-early 1980s after combine harvesters left residue behind.
In-situ options: Happy Seeders, Super Seeders, rotavators; ex-situ: bio-ethanol and compressed biogas.
Parliamentary Committee on air quality said penalising farmers should be a last resort.

Tax devolution — Finance Commission.page: 16th Finance Commission, Members, Period, Recommendations, Impact
facts: Finance Commission is constituted every five years under Article 280; 16th FC, chaired by Arvind Panagariya, covers 2026-27 to 2030-31.
16th FC retained States’ 41% share of the divisible pool, which excludes collection cost, cesses and surcharges.
16th FC weights: income distance 42.5%, population (2011) 17.5%, area 10%, forest 10%, demographic performance 10%, GDP contribution 10%.
16th FC fixed States’ annual fiscal deficit ceiling at 3% of GSDP and asked to end off-budget borrowings.

Tropical cyclones — naming, Bay of Benga.page: Cyclones, Meaning, Types, Cyclogenesis Mechanism, Impacts
facts: North Indian Ocean names are managed by the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones; system introduced in September 2004.
The panel has 13 member countries; RSMC New Delhi names cyclones sequentially, column-wise, from the approved list.
IMD scale: Cyclonic Storm 62-88 km/h; Severe 89-117 km/h; Very Severe 118-166 km/h.
